headline: Avoiding Common Mistakes When Widening a Doorway
articleBody:
Widening a doorway can make a huge difference in how your home feels, but it's a project where a few common mistakes can quickly lead to bigger headaches. Knowing what to watch out for can save you time, money, and a lot of frustration. Let's go over some of the biggest pitfalls we see.

One of the most frequent errors is underestimating structural support needs. People often don't realize if a wall is load-bearing, and simply removing studs without proper headers can compromise your home's integrity. Always, always verify if it's load-bearing and plan for the right support. Another big one is failing to locate concealed utilities before demolition. Hitting a water pipe or an electrical line isn't just messy; it can be dangerous and expensive to fix. A thorough assessment before any demolition starts is absolutely critical.

Many folks also forget that widening a doorway creates a cascade of follow-on work. You're not just moving a wall; you're often creating new needs for flooring, casing, and paint. The new opening will likely impact the surrounding finishes, so plan for those touch-ups and replacements from the get-go. Lastly, ignoring permit requirements for structural changes or changes that affect egress or accessibility can cause significant issues down the road. Local building codes are there for a reason, and getting the necessary permits and inspections ensures your project is safe and compliant.
